The work

Some things have to be experienced.

Intimacy cannot be learned from a distance. Neither can trust, surrender or presence. They are lived capacities—revealed in the moments when we allow ourselves to be seen, affected, challenged and met.

Rina creates carefully held experiences in which the body, relationship, ritual and attention become part of the inquiry. There is nothing to perform and no ideal self to become. The invitation is to meet what is already here more honestly—and discover what becomes possible from there.

Meet Rina Trevi, your guide.

A practice shaped by many worlds.

Rina Trevi is an artist, guide and author whose work explores intimacy, embodiment, power and surrender through direct experience.

She is the originator of Shibari as Ritual, a distinct approach to rope rooted in somatic attunement, meditation, vulnerability and deep relational presence.

Her guidance draws on nearly two decades of meditation and Tantric practice, extensive experience in power exchange, and training in trauma and somatics, coaching and relational work. Whether working with individuals, couples or practitioners, she creates carefully held spaces for people to explore beyond the familiar—and meet themselves and one another with greater honesty and presence.

Begin where you are

You do not need to know exactly what you are looking for.

You may be drawn to a private experience, a deeper professional practice or an immersive weekend with others.

Explore the available pathways—or get in touch if you are unsure where to begin.

Contact Rina

Private work

A private space for inquiry, learning and embodied encounter.

Some forms of private work develop skill. Others offer space for insight, release and greater wholeness.

Private work with Rina can take the form of a focused coaching series, an individual study or a singular ceremony. Each pathway is shaped around your intentions, experience and boundaries.

Three ways to enter

Focused Coaching

Four private remote sessions centered on a meaningful question, recurring pattern, relationship or life transition.

Coaching combines dialogue, somatic inquiry and reflective practices, with optional guided self-tying when bringing the inquiry into the body would be useful.

Private Studies

A focused course of learning for individuals or couples who want to develop an embodied practice with depth and personal guidance.

Studies may explore foundational Shibari, rope as a ritual of containment, intentional touch, embodied intimacy or bodywork—whether for personal exploration, relational deepening or professional application.

The pace and direction are shaped around what you want to learn and how you hope to bring it into your life or work.

Private Ceremonies

A singular, carefully prepared experience created around an intention, transition or desire to encounter something beyond the familiar.

Ceremonies may take the form of a private rope journey or the Sacred Feminine Touch Ceremony. These are not performances or conventional sessions, but immersive encounters with attention, vulnerability, sensation and surrender.

Focused coaching

Four conversations. One meaningful place to begin.

You may understand a situation intellectually and still find yourself repeating the same response. You may feel disconnected from your body, uncertain about what you want or dissatisfied with a life that appears functional from the outside.

The Focused Coaching Series offers four private remote sessions in which we stay with one question, pattern, relationship or transition long enough to understand what is shaping it—and allow a different response to emerge.

Sessions may combine extended dialogue, somatic inquiry, meditation, imagery and practices for reflection between meetings. When useful, Rina may also guide you through simple self-tying exercises, allowing questions of boundaries, support, control, resistance or surrender to be explored through the body.

No rope experience is required, and the use of rope is always optional.

The intention is to help you move from confusion, disconnection or stagnation toward greater clarity, agency, connection and aliveness—without creating an indefinite weekly commitment.

Inquire about focused coaching

Private studies

Sacred Feminine Touch & Embodied Intimacy

Sacred Feminine Touch is an original modality created by Rina—a form of ceremonial bodywork shaped by nearly two decades of Tantric study and practice, and centered on presence, receptivity and devotional touch.

Studies may explore creating safety and trust, communicating desires and boundaries, working with breath and sensation, and offering touch that is attentive, reverent and free from pressure to perform or progress sexually.

This path is open to individuals, couples and practitioners exploring the work for personal, relational or professional reasons.

Inquire about private studies

Private ceremonies

Creating safe spaces for self-discovery, release and transformation.

Each private ceremony is structured around Rina’s Four Ins: Intake, Intention, In-Space and Integration.

Intake

We begin by taking time to know you—your history, present circumstances, boundaries and what is drawing you toward the experience.

Intention

Together, we clarify the deeper why behind the journey. This intention becomes its guiding star: a point of orientation without predetermining what must happen.

In-Space

The in-person ceremony unfolds within an intentionally prepared environment. Rather than following a fixed script, Rina responds to what emerges through the body, the relationship and the experience itself.

Integration

The journey concludes with a post-session conversation. Together, we reflect on what occurred, give language to emerging insights and consider how they might become tangible choices or actions in your life.

Private ceremony

Private Rope Journey

A one-to-one ceremonial experience using rope as a container for self-discovery, meditation and embodied exploration.

The journey may include rope, breath, music, stillness, movement, sensation and guided inquiry. Depending on your intention and experience, the rope may remain floor-based or include partial or full suspension.

People enter these journeys for many reasons: to explore surrender or control, move through a personal threshold, encounter an emotion through the body, deepen self-trust or experience being held without having to remain composed.

No previous experience with Shibari is required.

Private ceremony

Sacred Feminine Touch Ceremony

Sacred Feminine Touch is Rina’s original ceremonial bodywork modality, created for people of all genders and shaped by nearly two decades of Tantric study and practice. Here, feminine refers to the receptive dimension of experience rather than the gender of the recipient.

Rather than isolating one area of the body or approaching the person as something to be corrected, the ceremony engages the whole being. Breath, presence and attentive touch create space to deepen receptivity and expand the body’s natural capacity for sensation, pleasure and connection.

For some, the journey allows held emotion or trauma-related patterns to surface and soften. For others, it becomes a nourishing expansion into tenderness, aliveness and bliss. Often, both movements belong to the same experience.

There is no required response and no particular state to achieve. The body is invited to unfold at its own pace, within clearly established boundaries and ongoing consent.

Your inquiry begins a conversation about what you are seeking, your previous experience, relevant boundaries and which form of private work may be most appropriate.

Rituals of Containment

Private Practitioner Mentorship

A 30-hour private mentorship for therapists, coaches, bodyworkers and embodiment practitioners who want to integrate rope into carefully held therapeutic and transformational work.

This is not a conventional Shibari training.

Technical rope is part of the work, but it is not its primary subject. The mentorship focuses on using simple rope as a structure for presence, containment, nervous-system attunement and embodied exploration.

The rope stays simple.
The presence goes deep.

Apply for the mentorship

Who this is for

For practitioners who work where words are not always enough.

Rituals of Containment is designed for people who already accompany others through emotional, relational, somatic or transformational processes and want to explore how rope can become part of that work.

The mentorship may be appropriate for:

  • Therapists and counselors
  • Coaches
  • Somatic and embodiment practitioners
  • Bodyworkers
  • Intimacy practitioners
  • Facilitators and ceremonial guides
  • Shibari practitioners seeking a more trauma-aware and integrative approach

You do not need to be an advanced rope practitioner. Foundational rope skills can be developed within the mentorship.

What matters is your willingness to work with care, remain present with complexity and examine how your own nervous system, intentions and relational patterns enter the space you create for another person.

Apply for the mentorship

The method

The work is first experienced through your own body.

The mentorship begins with you receiving a complete Rituals of Containment journey. Before learning to guide another person, you experience the method from within—its structure, vulnerability, intensity and need for careful integration.

From there, we move into the central frameworks of the work:

The Four Ins

Intake, Intention, In-Space and Integration—a structure for preparing, guiding and completing an embodied journey.

Consent as Self-Trust

Moving beyond permission-based consent toward an ongoing practice of bodily awareness, communication, choice and the capacity to change course.

Trauma-Aware Facilitation

Recognizing activation, protective responses and overwhelm; understanding when to remain with an experience, when to reduce intensity and when the work has moved beyond your professional scope.

The Wheel of Ritual Presence

A framework for working with attention, relationship, environment, intention and the practitioner’s own state.

Rope Somatics

Using pressure, structure, movement and stillness to support awareness of sensation, emotion and nervous-system response.

Elemental Rope Flow

Working with different qualities of contact and intensity—from grounding and containment to movement, challenge, expansion and release.

Language, Inquiry & Suggestion

Integrating contemplative self-inquiry, individualized verbal anchors, affirmation, hypnotic language and archetypal journeys without imposing meaning on the recipient’s experience.

Eros, Power & Professional Boundaries

Understanding how attraction, projection, power and intimacy may enter the space—and how to meet them with clarity and responsibility.

Closure & Integration

Bringing an experience to completion through aftercare, reflection and practices that help insight become part of life rather than remain an isolated moment of intensity.

What makes this different

The rope is visible. Much of the work is not.

Most rope education focuses on technique, visual form, performance or scene dynamics. Rituals of Containment focuses on what is happening underneath—and on the practitioner’s capacity to perceive and respond to it.

  • How do you create enough safety for someone to soften without deciding what their experience should become?
  • How do you recognize when intensity is useful—and when it is becoming too much?
  • How do you remain present with emotion without trying to fix, interpret or prematurely resolve it?
  • How do you work responsibly with power, intimacy and eros without becoming lost in projection, gratification or shame?
  • How do you distinguish meaningful challenge from reenactment or overwhelm?
  • How do you bring a deep experience to completion so that it becomes integrated rather than merely intense?

Transformation does not occur simply because something dramatic happens. It becomes possible when a person feels sufficiently held to encounter what is real—and when the practitioner has the discernment not to force what is not ready.

How the mentorship unfolds

Thirty hours of private, individualized work.

This is not a group curriculum delivered on a fixed schedule. The mentorship is shaped around your professional background, existing rope experience and intended application of the method.

The 30 hours include:

Personal experience

Receiving the work yourself and reflecting on what becomes visible from inside the container.

Foundational rope practice

Developing the safety, handling and technical skills needed to use simple rope with confidence and care.

Frameworks & demonstration

Studying the core methodology and observing how its principles are applied in practice.

Supervised facilitation

Practicing the work with guidance, feedback and attention to your presence, pacing, language and decision-making.

Professional application

Considering how the method may—and may not—fit within your existing work, training, ethics and scope of practice.

Integration & assessment

Reflecting on your development, identifying areas that require further practice and establishing how you will carry the work forward responsibly.

The mentorship may be completed as an intensive or distributed across a longer period, depending on location, experience and availability.

Completion & investment

Investment

$12,000

A private professional mentorship in Rina Trevi’s signature method.

The mentorship includes 30 hours of individualized study, personal experience, instruction, supervised practice and integration.

Upon successful completion, you will receive a certificate of completion in the Rituals of Containment method.

This certificate recognizes your study of Rina’s approach. It does not replace clinical licensure, accredited therapeutic education or any training required within your existing professional scope. You remain responsible for practicing within your competence, qualifications and local professional regulations.

The mentorship is offered selectively to a limited number of practitioners each year.

Applications are considered based on professional background, intention, readiness for personal embodiment and the ethical fit between the method and your existing work.

Apply for the mentorship

Before you apply

Depth requires discernment.

This mentorship is not designed for those seeking:

  • Advanced suspension or performance-focused rope training
  • A rapid certification without personal embodiment and supervised practice
  • A fixed protocol to apply identically to every client
  • A way to work beyond their existing professional competence or scope
  • Intensity for its own sake

It is for practitioners who are willing to examine their own relationship with power, control, intimacy, uncertainty and responsibility—not only learn how to guide another person through theirs.

The invitation

Rituals of Containment approaches rope not as control, but as structure.

Not as spectacle, but as attention.

Not as an escape from the body, but as a way of listening more closely to it.

For practitioners ready to bring greater presence, discernment and embodied intelligence into their work, this mentorship offers a rigorous and deeply personal foundation.

Apply for the private mentorship

Intimately Tied

A weekend immersion in intimate leadership and empowered surrender.

Intimately Tied is a small-group experience for individuals and couples who want to explore attention, communication, trust and embodied intimacy through rope.

Across the weekend, participants move between learning, guided practice, personal exploration and shared experience. You may come alone or with a partner, and no previous rope experience is required.

Offered two to three times each year in selected locations.

About Rina

A practice shaped by many worlds.

Rina Trevi is an artist, guide and author whose work explores intimacy, embodiment, power and surrender through direct experience.

Her work has never belonged neatly to a single discipline. It moves between conversation and the body, psychological inquiry and ceremonial practice, structure and spontaneity. Depending on the person and the purpose, she may work with dialogue, silence, touch, rope, meditation or carefully designed embodied experience.

What remains consistent is the quality of the space she creates: attentive, direct, deeply human and spacious enough for what is usually managed or concealed to become visible.

Rina does not offer an ideal self to aspire to. She invites people to meet what is already here—with greater honesty, curiosity and capacity to remain present.

Her approach is shaped not only by formal study, but by nearly two decades of personal practice and an unconventional life lived across cultures, identities and edges.

A life outside conventional paths

The expected life—and the decision to leave it.

Rina grew up in post-Soviet Russia, in an environment shaped by silence, secrecy and strong expectations about who a person should become.

At eighteen, she immigrated to the United States and began constructing an entirely different life. She earned an MBA, entered corporate finance and achieved a version of success that appeared convincing from the outside.

Her body gave a different answer.

Exhaustion and a growing sense of estrangement made it impossible to continue treating competence as fulfillment. Rina left the corporate path and began traveling through Asia, studying meditation, Tantra and alternative approaches to healing and human development.

What began as a search for a more authentic life gradually became a lifelong inquiry:

What happens when we stop organizing ourselves around what is acceptable—and begin listening to what is true?

That question has carried Rina through multiple countries, professions, identities and forms of practice. It remains at the center of her work today.

Power, projection & the hidden self

Twelve years inside the dynamics of control and surrender.

For twelve years, Rina worked internationally as a professional Dominatrix.

Behind the ritual and theatricality of that world, she gained an unusual view into what people reveal when their public identities are no longer in the room. She worked closely with desire, shame, fantasy, control, surrender and the parts of the self that rarely find expression in ordinary life.

Those years taught her that power is never merely about who appears to hold it. Control can protect vulnerability. Surrender can require profound agency and self-trust. Intensity can create honesty—but without discernment, it can also reinforce the very patterns a person hopes to move beyond.

Over time, the conventional role of Dominatrix became too narrow for the work Rina was actually doing. Her sessions increasingly drew upon meditation, self-inquiry, somatic awareness and ritual, becoming less about fulfilling a prescribed fantasy and more about discovering what the fantasy was asking to reveal.

That chapter remains an important foundation of her work, but no longer defines its limits. What began in the language of power exchange gradually evolved into a broader practice of helping people meet themselves beyond performance, protection and familiar identity.

Meditation, Tantra & Shibari

Where discipline meets devotion.

Rina began studying meditation and Tantra at twenty-one. What followed was nearly two decades of practice across Asia and the United States, including repeated silent Vipassana retreats, contemplative self-inquiry and the ongoing discipline of daily meditation.

These traditions gave her a language for attention, impermanence and the possibility of meeting experience without immediately resisting, controlling or explaining it.

Shibari entered her life later and brought many of these threads together.

For nearly a decade, Rina has studied rope with Bodhi Zapha, within the Osada Steve lineage, as well as Tati Limati and Ren Yagami. Through receiving, practicing and eventually teaching, she came to understand rope not only as technique or visual form, but as a structure through which attention, vulnerability, trust and surrender could become tangible.

From this emerged Shibari as Ritual, Rina’s distinct approach to rope rooted in meditative presence, somatic attunement, emotional honesty and relational care.

In this work, rope does not create the experience by itself. It gives form to what is already present—a boundary, a longing, a resistance, a need to be held or a readiness to let go.

Training & professional foundation

Experience supported by study.

Rina’s work has been shaped through long-term personal practice, apprenticeship and direct experience, alongside formal training across several disciplines.

Her training and education include:

Embodiment & relational work

  • Trauma and Somatics
  • Female Reproductive Massage
  • Tantric bodywork and intimacy practices
  • Consent, nervous-system awareness and embodied facilitation

Coaching & guided inquiry

  • Life Coaching
  • Neuro-Linguistic Programming
  • Hypnotherapy
  • Quantum Time Technique
  • Meditation and contemplative self-inquiry

Ceremony & life transitions

  • Death Doula training
  • Life-Cycle Celebrant training
  • Ritual design and integration

Education & organizational experience

  • Master of Business Administration
  • Professional background in corporate finance
  • Experience creating and leading private mentorships, group immersions and practitioner education

No single certification defines Rina’s approach. Its depth comes from the way these disciplines have been practiced, questioned and integrated over time.

Rina’s work is educational, developmental and experiential. She is not a psychotherapist or medical provider, and her services are not a substitute for licensed mental-health or medical care.

Beyond the work

Drawn equally to stillness and intensity.

Rina’s life has moved between silent meditation retreats and extreme sports, long periods of travel and the search for home, disciplined practice and encounters with the unknown.

She is a skydiver, BASE jumper and freediver, as well as a lifelong student of contemplative and mystical traditions. Her curiosity has led her through Vipassana, Tantra, Tibetan Buddhism, Sufism and various shamanic traditions.

She is equally drawn to quieter forms of attention: yoga, music, time in nature and the ordinary intimacy of a life lived slowly.

These worlds continue to shape her understanding of fear, trust, surrender and what it means to feel fully alive.

Where the work lives now

Today, Rina works privately with individuals and couples, mentors therapists and embodiment practitioners, and facilitates a small number of immersive weekends each year.

The forms vary, but the invitation remains the same: to move beyond explanation, meet what is present more honestly and discover what becomes possible from there.

Experiences

In their own words.

The work is different for every person who enters it.

Some come with a clear intention. Others arrive with a question they cannot yet name. What follows may be quiet or intense, clarifying or disorienting, immediately understood or revealed gradually through integration.

These are reflections from people who have experienced Rina’s work through coaching, private ceremonies, embodied study, mentorship and group immersion.

Their experiences are their own. They are shared not as promises of a particular outcome, but as glimpses into what became possible within the work.

Focused Coaching

Ariane WilliamsPrivate Coaching Client

“Rina is a phenomenal intimacy and vulnerability coach with over a decade of experience in Tantric arts and spiritual practices.

I’ve worked with her for three years in various capacities, and she has helped me navigate and integrate so many things in my life.

Working with her has helped me build confidence in who I am and connect more deeply with my inner truth and strengths. She has also helped me develop a deeper understanding of my body and my relationship with it, enabling me to feel safety in my body in ways I’m not sure I experienced before working with her.

If you’re interested in exploring yourself in different ways, I highly recommend working with her.”

ThierryPrivate Coaching Client

“When I began this vulnerability coaching journey with Rina, I wasn’t sure exactly what I was looking for. I wanted to open to vulnerability, learn how to find and meet my fears, and connect more deeply with my inner self so that I could give more love to those around me.

The extent of my learning has been amazing and exhilarating—well beyond my expectations.

I moved from having strong self-esteem toward better loving myself and, as a result, loving those around me and life in all its forms. Through meditative work, I met my inner child and brought him tenderness, compassion and love. I can now dive into myself, feel safe and face my fears, hopes, light and darkness while valuing them all.

I thought I was a mighty oak and discovered that I am a reed. I feel more humble, but also stronger and more complete.

Even though we worked entirely online, between Thailand and Europe, we were together in the journey. This was teamwork at its best.

I felt safe throughout and appreciated Rina’s empathy, generosity, skill and commitment.”

Private Rope Journeys

Poppy Love SauvagePrivate Shibari Journey & Mentorship

“This was a full-on shamanic journey.

I came with the intention to expand my capacity, deepen my surrender and meet my edges in my body.

Mission accomplished.

Three suspensions. Intense, confronting and incredibly beautiful.

What stayed with me most was something Rina shared before we began: an invitation to release the dualistic lens of pain versus pleasure—to meet sensation as sensation, without labeling it and without story.

That shifted everything.

I stayed with my breath.
I stayed in my body.

Deeply empowering.
Deeply liberating.

I feel immense gratitude for Rina and her ability to hold me through something so cathartic, empowering and liberating.”

Amy EdwardsPodcast Host & Private Shibari Journey Participant

“When I was in the Shibari space with you, there was this element of cosmic openness.

One of the things that surprised me was how meditative the experience was. I didn’t know what to expect. Perhaps I thought it would be more sexual because the only bondage situations I had experienced before were sexual. For me, it had sensuality, but it was much more meditative.

It became another way of diving into my vulnerability.

I’m naturally curious, and that curiosity brought me here. I wondered what the experience might open within me.

I loved the binding and not needing to make decisions. The touch was so comforting, and I value the whole experience deeply. It was a truly safe space, and it freed me in an entirely different way.”

Watch our conversation on The Amy Edwards Show

ArnoldPrivate Shibari Journey Participant

“After some reflection, the best way I can describe the journey is that it allowed me to escape my own thoughts and simply be.

I know Shibari journeys sometimes compel people to confront their shadows, but for me, particularly in the calm moments, it brings a sense of tranquility.

The more intense moments remain beneficial. They contrast with the pleasurable moments, allowing me to value those more deeply, while also helping me confront emotions I generally repress—particularly anger.

I find it interesting that being vulnerable in rope diminishes my anxiety, while for others it may bring them closer to their fears.

I also cherish the intimacy of the experience and the presence you foster. I feel more intimacy through these journeys with you than I have found through encounters that were only physical.”

Sacred Feminine Touch & Ceremonial Bodywork

Alison CharlesSacred Feminine Touch Ceremony

“Receiving this bodywork was the result of a prayer I had carried for two and a half years. I patiently waited for the right guide to appear.

I could feel that an entirely different world wanted to open in terms of new ways of experiencing intimacy—Dharmic rather than karmic.

The overall journey lasted from noon until five. Alongside the bodywork, other rituals and a tea ceremony were interwoven. A primary reason I entered the experience was to release old energies. What emerged included anger, rage and shame, all held with the utmost reverence.

So much happened in this journey.

The final message I heard as we wrapped was: ‘Forever changed.’

Evidence of that appeared the following morning when I went outside and everything looked different. I heard: ‘The filter of anger has been removed.’”

Jackson DouglasTantric Bodywork Journey

“My journey with Rina was deeply transformative and entirely unexpected.

Before our session, I was nervous and uncertain about what was to come. But I had felt called to this practice for many years, so I knew I had to have faith and be prepared to surrender.

I entered with the intention of deepening my capacity for self-love and learning to transform lust into reverence.

The session transcended those intentions and showed me that surrendering control was the answer to my uncertainty. The experience went far deeper than anything I could have expected.

Rina’s practice and the container she creates are emotionally tender and intensely alive. Throughout the process, I encountered a vast range of feelings and saw aspects of myself I had not previously uncovered.

I left feeling a deep and gracious reverence for myself and for life.”

Professional Study

Andre LazarusSex Coach & Sacred Feminine Touch Practitioner Training Participant

“The space that Rina held was exceptional.

I felt the responsibility of coming into this offering while knowing that there are many places in the world where men take up space. I had to ask myself whether this was a place where I should be.

I checked in with myself repeatedly, and the answer was yes.

What drew me toward the work was an opportunity to honor women and their spirit, while sharing my love for caring for and nurturing human bodies.

The training deepened my existing knowledge, particularly around pressure points, abdominal massage and preparing someone’s body for a deeper intimate experience. It also expanded my understanding of what a person can ask for and receive.

Intimate touch does not have to progress into a sexual realm.”
